review_comments:
I think all these tests should be made to target both stream-based and string-based serialization, since reference preservation logic contains bespoke async code.

If anything, that's more feedback on the design of the base [SerializerTests](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/9030b78f19b363da4ffcaa00d8ae4929b010fd48/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/tests/Common/SerializerTests.cs#L8-L10) class. I don't think we should have separate entrypoints for "stream" and "string", since both can be abstracted behind a single serializer interface (effectively the `JsonSerializerWrapperForString` API). The different modalities can then be tested separately using `ReferenceHandlerTests_Sync` or `ReferenceHandlerTests_Async` derived classes that specify only one SUT.

[We already do this in a few other places](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/tests/System.Text.Json.Tests/Serialization/JsonSerializerWrapperForString.cs#L123) but we're far from being consistent.
Agreed. Per offline discussion, we'll leave this PR to simply share the tests as-is with src-gen, then tackle this with https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/66463.
Nice. I was literally planning on making that change myself today. Great minds and all that
Guessing the build failures are related to missing Newtonsoft references in the SourceGen test project?
Yup they were moved to `tests/Common/TestClasses/TestClasses.cs` for easier sharing with the src-gen test project.
